# FlowRead Access: shared contract

This is the contract every agent builds against. If you need to change it, write down the change in your final report and don't edit this file. The lead owns it.

## Product in one line
An accessibility office uploads a course PDF or DOCX. FlowRead converts it into a structured, accessible document, and staff review it. Each student then reads it with a profile: Dyslexia, ADHD/Focus, Screen reader or Low vision.

## AccessDoc (JSON)

```jsonc
{
  "id": "doc_<random>",            // generated by backend (uuid4 hex, prefixed)
  "title": "Week 3: Cell Biology",
  "lang": "en",                     // BCP-47
  "sourceFile": "week3.pdf",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-23T20:00:00Z",
  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "s1",
      "heading": "Introduction",    // "" for the untitled first section
      "level": 2,                   // the heading level of this section's heading (1-6); the doc title is h1
      "summary": null,              // string once fetched or generated
      "blocks": [ /* Block[] */ ]
    }
  ],
  "report": { /* Report, see below */ }
}
```

### Blocks
Every block has `id` (unique in the doc, e.g. `"b12"`), `type`, and an optional `plain` (a plain-language rewrite, `null` until requested). Section headings are **not** repeated as blocks. Sub-headings inside a section are `heading` blocks.

| type | fields |
|---|---|
| `heading` | `text`, `level` (2–6) |
| `paragraph` | `text` |
| `list` | `ordered` (bool), `items` (string[]) |
| `table` | `caption` (string\|null), `headers` (string[]; empty array = no header row detected), `rows` (string[][]) |
| `image` | `src` (data URL, png/jpeg, downscaled to max 1200px), `alt` (string), `altStatus` (`"ai"` \| `"approved"` \| `"decorative"` \| `"missing"`), `caption` (string\|null) |
| `math` | `latex` (string\|null), `spoken` (plain-English reading of the expression), `text` (raw extracted text) |
| `pageMarker` | `n` (source page number; for "page 12 in your printed copy" navigation) |

Text fields are plain text (no HTML). Renderers must escape them.

### Report
```jsonc
{
  "score": 87,                     // 0-100, 100 = no issues
  "issues": [
    { "blockId": "b7", "sectionId": "s2", "rule": "image-alt-unreviewed", "severity": "serious", "message": "AI image description has not been reviewed by staff." }
  ]
}
```
Rules: `image-alt-missing` (critical), `image-alt-unreviewed` (serious, altStatus `ai`), `heading-skip` (moderate), `table-no-headers` (serious), `doc-missing-title` (serious), `doc-missing-lang` (serious), `section-too-long` (minor, over about 1500 words), `math-no-spoken` (moderate).
Score = max(0, 100 − 15·critical − 8·serious − 4·moderate − 1·minor).
The frontend must be able to recompute the report locally, so `frontend/src/access/shared/check.js` mirrors `backend/access/check.py`. Same rules, same scoring.

## API (FastAPI, prefix `/api/access`)

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/access/convert` | multipart `file` (pdf/docx), optional form field `describeImages` (`"true"` default) | **SSE** `text/event-stream`. Events: `data: {"type":"progress","step":"layout"\|"tables"\|"images"\|"structure"\|"check","message":"Reading page layout…","pct":0-100}` … then `data: {"type":"done","doc":AccessDoc}` or `data: {"type":"error","message":"…"}` |
| POST | `/api/access/plain` | `{ "text": "...", "context": "section heading (optional)" }` | `{ "plain": "..." }` |
| POST | `/api/access/summary` | `{ "heading": "...", "text": "..." }` | `{ "summary": "2-3 sentence summary" }` |
| POST | `/api/access/describe-image` | `{ "src": "data:image/png;base64,...", "context": "nearby text" }` | `{ "alt": "...", "decorative": false }` |
| POST | `/api/access/check` | `AccessDoc` | `Report` |

- Missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` means **conversion still works**. Images get `alt: ""` and `altStatus: "missing"`, and `plain`/`summary`/`describe-image` return 503 with a clear `detail`.
- Uploads are capped at 25 MB, returning 413 if larger.
- The frontend reads the SSE stream with `fetch` + `ReadableStream` (POST), the same as `hooks/useSummarize.js`.

## Frontend layout (React 19 + Vite + react-router 7)

Routes (the lead wires them in `src/main.jsx`):
- `/access`: staff landing (Agent 2)
- `/access/new`: upload and convert (Agent 2)
- `/access/review/:id`: staff review and publish (Agent 2)
- `/read/:id`: student reader (Agent 3)

Default exports the lead imports:
- `src/access/staff/AccessLanding.jsx`
- `src/access/staff/NewConversion.jsx`
- `src/access/staff/ReviewPage.jsx`
- `src/access/reader/StudentReader.jsx`

Shared modules (**Agent 3 owns** `src/access/shared/`. Agent 2 imports them and doesn't edit them. Agent 3 should create these **first** so Agent 2 can import early):
- `shared/storage.js`: `listDocs()`, `getDoc(id)`, `saveDoc(doc)`, `deleteDoc(id)`. Uses localStorage key `flowread-access:docs` (a map id→doc), with every access wrapped in try/catch and a quota error surfaced as a thrown `Error('Storage full')`.
- `shared/check.js`: `checkDoc(doc) → Report` (mirrors the backend).
- `shared/api.js`: `convertFile(file, {onProgress}) → Promise<AccessDoc>`, `plainLanguage(text, context)`, `summarizeSection(heading, text)`, `describeImage(src, context)`. Uses `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:8000'`.
- `shared/DocRenderer.jsx`: semantic renderer `({doc, sections?, profile, onRequestPlain}) `. Agent 2 uses it for the review preview.
- `shared/exportHtml.js`: `exportAccessibleHtml(doc) → string`, a complete self-contained HTML file with the reader CSS and a small vanilla JS profile switcher inlined. No network needed.
- `shared/profiles.js`: profile presets (`dyslexia`, `focus`, `screenreader`, `lowvision`, `standard`).

Existing app (`/`, `/reader`, `src/components`, `src/hooks`, `src/pages`) must keep working. You may **import** from `src/hooks` and `src/components` (e.g. `useTTS`), but don't edit them.

Styling: use CSS variables from `src/styles/themes.css` (`--bg`, `--text`, `--accent`, `--border`, …, plus fonts `--font-body`, `--font-dyslexic`, `--font-atkinson`). New CSS goes in your own directory (`*.css` files imported by your components).

## Accessibility bar (what QA tests)
- axe-core: zero `serious` or `critical` violations on every route and every profile.
- All functions work by keyboard alone. Focus is always visible. Skip link to `<main>`.
- One `<h1>` per page and no skipped heading levels in the rendered doc.
- At 200% text / 320 CSS px width there's no horizontal scrolling (except inside data tables, which scroll in their own container with `tabindex="0"` and a label).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected. The screen-reader profile has no motion at all.
- Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in every theme.

## Ground rules
- Edit only the directories you own. The lead owns `src/main.jsx`, `backend/main.py`, `package.json`, `requirements.txt` and this file. If you need a dependency, say so in your report and don't install it.
- Commit only your own files to branch `pivot/access` (`git add <your paths>`, never `git add -A`). Never push. Never commit `.env`.
- Don't use the term "Bionic Reading" (it's a registered trademark). Say "bold word starts".
- Make no medical claims ("supports", not "treats").
- All fixtures and sample docs must be synthetic. No copyrighted material.
